text:
sarah: FYI — NVD posted CVE-2026-31415 for protobuf-java (deserialization -> memory corruption, possible RCE). Link: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-31415  EPSS: 0.12, CVSS: 7.8 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H). Our SBOM shows protobuf-java 3.14.x in a few services.

jamal: thanks. which services are on those versions? can we get a quick inventory?

olga: ran `rg 'com.google.protobuf:protobuf-java' -S services | sed -n '1,50p'` — quick hits:

```
services/ingestion/pom.xml: <version>3.14.2</version>
services/telemetry/build.gradle: implementation 'com.google.protobuf:protobuf-java:3.11.0'
services/batch-exporter/pom.xml: <version>3.14.0</version>
```

sarah: good. exploitability check — any public PoC yet?

sec-bot: [automated] EPSS pulled 2026-03-20T08:11Z: 0.12. No Github PoC observed. Tags: serialization, memory-corruption.

jamal: no PoC seen. Given CVSS 7.8 but no PoC, lean P2 (patch within 72h). Recommend upgrading to the latest 3.19.x which includes the crash fix. Can we canary ingestion first?

mike: ingestion runs on Dedicated US-WEST pool. Low traffic window 01:00-03:00 UTC. We can schedule a canary then. As short-term mitigation we should restrict external access to the ingestion listener for 48hrs.

olga: mitigation checklist (short):
1) Apply k8s NetworkPolicy to block external access to port 8080 for ingestion.
2) Raise parsing/audit logging level for ingestion to DEBUG for 48h.
3) Add temporary RBAC role `ingestion-restricted` that forces auth on public endpoints (deny unauthenticated payloads).
I'll open PRs for 1+3.

sarah: also check KMS question — does ingestion verify signatures via KMS or local secret? If KMS-verified we're less exposed.

jamal: ingestion currently verifies HMAC with a Vault-managed symmetric key (not KMS signing). Rotating Vault keys is low value right now; migration to KMS-backed signing is a roadmap item for Q2. For now focus on patch + network lockdown.

sarah: action items: (1) jamal -> open upgrade PR for ingestion canary + tests, tag olga for network changes; (2) olga -> apply NetworkPolicy and RBAC change, open ENGSEC ticket; (3) mike -> schedule canary in next maintenance window (01:00-03:00 UTC); (4) sec-bot -> post follow-up if PoC appears. Target: full patch deploy if canary stable within 72h. :thumbsup: 

olga: creating ENGSEC-4387 now, will link PRs and k8s manifests. :eyes: 

jamal: starting the PR. tagging @olga for review.

sarah: thanks team — post any blockers or test failures here so we can escalate.
